about: The design principles the guide offers before any value is chosen. The owner fixes three to five, from this list or in words of their own. A principle here says which option of a layer's choice it favours and why, so a recommendation can rest on it without a model: `choice` is a choice key of layers.json and `option` one of its options. `suits` lists the product types the guide offers it for first; any principle may be picked for any product. A principle in the owner's own words is recorded and can be cited, but no option follows from it.

principles.name: dense and scannable
principles.statement: A screen shows as much as a person can scan at once: space goes to content, and the steps of type stay close.

favours.why: related steps let headings stay close to the body text without blurring
gentle steps keep many levels of heading on one working screen
small corners keep tight rows and cells from looking crowded

principles.name: context stays in view
principles.statement: Where a person came from stays in view: opening a record never hides the list it came from.

favours.why: the record opens next to the list, so the list stays where it was

principles.name: one task at a time
principles.statement: A screen asks for one task at a time: what is open takes the whole view.

favours.why: the record takes the place of the list, so nothing else competes with it

principles.name: clear hierarchy
principles.statement: The order of importance is seen before it is read: each level of heading steps up clearly.

favours.why: every size comes from one ratio, so each step is a visible step
clear steps that still fit a working screen

principles.name: reading comes first
principles.statement: Long text reads easily: generous steps of type, and nothing pulls the eye away from the words.

favours.why: a scale from one ratio gives long text a rhythm of headings
strong steps suit pages with few levels of heading
a text opened in place has the whole width to be read in

principles.name: soft and approachable
principles.statement: Shapes feel soft and friendly: rounded corners, nothing sharp.

favours.why: large corners read as soft at every size of control

principles.name: precise and technical
principles.statement: Shapes are exact and quiet: corners are square or nearly so.

favours.why: nearly square corners read as exact without looking unfinished

principles.name: readable for everyone
principles.statement: Everyone can read it: text and controls stay clear for people with low vision, even where that costs the brand colour.

favours.why: text needs a contrast ratio of 7:1 instead of 4.5:1

principles.name: familiar over novel
principles.statement: Familiar beats novel: the screens look and behave the way people already know.

favours.why: the sizes people have met in many products already
the corner the floor's components were drawn with
